items.title: Japan to sell lethal arms in move away from post-war pacifism
items.description: Japan has overhauled its decades-long defence export rule, allowing the country to sell lethal weapons internationally amid rising global tensions.

items.title: Seized Iranian ship Touska likely carried dual-use cargo, sources say

featured_image.name: Iran war updates: Uncertainty over talks, Trump says deal to come ‘quickly’

items.description: U.S. naval forces attacked and seized the Iranian-flagged cargo ship MV Touska on April 19 after a six-hour standoff in the Gulf of Oman, marking the first such enforcement action since the United States imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports on April 13. Iran condemned the seizure as "maritime piracy" and vowed military retaliation, pulling out of planned peace talks in Pakistan and casting doubt on a fragile ceasefire set to expire on April 21.[1][2]

items.title: Government to pay for showers for at-home aged care recipients
items.description: The decision to scrap the plan to charge older Australians $50/hour for showers was made after months of sustained criticism, including warnings that people were forgoing other care to afford the service.

items.title: UN climate chief warns of fossil-fuel stagflation at Berlin talks

featured_image.name: UN climate official Simon Stiell gives stark assessment

items.description: UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell warned on Tuesday that "fossil-fuel driven stagflation is now stalking economies," urging nations to accelerate clean energy adoption as the primary defense against rising temperatures and volatile energy costs. Speaking at the opening of the Petersberg Climate Dialogue in Berlin on April 21, Stiell described climate cooperation as essential to "fending off the twin-reapers of global heating and fossil fuel cost chaos."[1][2]

items.title: Curiosity rover detects 'origin-of-life' molecules on Mars

featured_image.name: Non-biologic Processes Don't Fully Explain Mars Organics

items.description: NASA's Curiosity rover has detected more than 20 organic molecules in clay-rich Martian rock, including compounds never before seen on the Red Planet, according to a study published on April 21 in the journal Nature Communications. The findings, drawn from a first-of-its-kind chemical experiment conducted remotely on Mars, offer fresh clues in the decades-long search for signs of ancient life beyond Earth.[1][2]

items.title: 'Everyone is scared': Captain caught at the world's shipping chokepoint speaks out
items.description: For months seafarers have been stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, tanker captain Raman Kapoor is speaking out about the fears and uncertainty of his crew.

items.title: Trump's Board of Peace in talks with DP World on Gaza rebuild

featured_image.name: Trump says Board of Peace will unveil $5B in Gaza ...

items.description: Representatives of Donald Trump's Board of Peace have held discussions with Dubai-based logistics giant DP World about managing supply chains and infrastructure projects in Gaza, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, in a move that underscores Washington's push to privatise key elements of the territory's rebuilding effort.[1]

items.title: Airbus agrees to acquire French cybersecurity firm Quarkslab

featured_image.name: Airbus bolsters cybersecurity capabilities with Quarkslab acquisition

items.description: Airbus announced on Monday that it has entered into an agreement to acquire Quarkslab, a French cybersecurity company, in a deal that extends the European aerospace giant's push to build sovereign cyber capabilities across the continent.

items.title: Rio Tinto posts higher Q1 iron ore sales, warns on Middle East risks

featured_image.name: Rio Tinto BHP Pilbara Iron Ore Partnership 200Mt Deal

items.description: Rio Tinto reported a 2.4% rise in first-quarter iron ore sales on Tuesday but cautioned that the ongoing conflict in the Middle East could disrupt its supply chains in the second half of 2026. The world's largest iron ore producer sold 72.4 million metric tons from its Pilbara operations in Western Australia during the three months ended March 31, up from 70.7 million tons a year earlier, though below the Visible Alpha consensus estimate of 74.6 million tons.[1][2]

items.title: Vanuatu warns Australia it will not be 'dictated to' after reports of China deal
items.description: As Australia presses on to finally sign a key agreement with Vanuatu, reports of a security agreement with China have drawn a fierce response from Port Vila.

items.title: Boyd says other AFL players are struggling 'under the surface' after Hollands episode
items.description: Tom Boyd, former AFL footballer turned mental health advocate, says the high-pressure environment of professional football means many players are struggling with mental health issues "under the surface".

items.title: States and territories left in the dark on NDIS savings
items.description: State treasurers say a meeting on NDIS reforms to be announced tomorrow was light on details, leaving states and territories waiting with everyone else to find out how a new round of savings measures will affect the disability scheme — and their budgets.

items.title: Japan scraps postwar ban on lethal weapons exports

featured_image.name: Japan's ruling party elects Sanae Takaichi as new leader ...

items.description: Japan's Cabinet on Tuesday approved the most sweeping overhaul of the country's defense export rules in decades, scrapping restrictions that had confined arms sales to non-combat equipment since the end of World War II. The decision opens the door for Japanese manufacturers to sell fighter jets, missiles, warships, and other lethal weapons on the global market for the first time.

items.title: Government pours $30m into counter-drone technology in wake of Iran war
items.description: The Australian government signs two contracts to develop counter-drone technology, including a laser that can track an object the size of a 10-cent coin travelling at more than 100 km/h.

items.title: China suddenly grants new beef licences to Australia
items.description: China has granted beef export approval to several new Australian facilities, just months after introducing a range of trade measures to protect its domestic cattle industry.

items.title: SpaceX begins Wall Street analyst briefings ahead of record $75B IPO

featured_image.name: SpaceX files confidentially for IPO targeting $1.75 trillion valuation

items.description:
SpaceX kicked off three days of private analyst meetings on Monday at its Starbase launch site in Boca Chica, Texas, as Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company moves closer to what would be the largest initial public offering in history, Reuters reported.[1][2]

The briefings, aimed at Wall Street's top aerospace and technology analysts, mark a key milestone in SpaceX's push to raise up to $75 billion and begin trading by late June. Executives are expected to lead an all-day meeting and tour at Starbase before offering analysts a visit to SpaceX's "Macrohard" xAI datacenter in Memphis, Tennessee, on April 23.[3][4][2]

items.title: Oil dips as Iran agrees to join U.S. peace talks in Islamabad

featured_image.name: US-Iran direct talks on ending war under way in Pakistan

items.description: Oil prices fell on Tuesday as expectations grew that the United States and Iran would resume peace negotiations in Pakistan this week, raising hopes for an easing of supply disruptions in the Middle East. The decline came after a volatile Monday session that saw crude surge on renewed tensions over the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Clean energy outpaced global electricity demand growth in 2025, Ember finds

featured_image.name: The State of Clean Energy, in 10 Charts - World Resources Institute

items.description:
Clean energy generation outpaced global electricity demand growth for the first time in 2025, powered by record solar expansion in China and India, according to energy think tank Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026, released on Monday.[1][2]

Clean power generation grew 887 terawatt hours last year, exceeding overall global electricity demand growth of 849 terawatt hours, the report found. Solar energy, which grew 30% in 2025, alone met three-quarters of the net rise in electricity demand, and combined with wind power generation, met 99% of it.[3][1]

items.description: Experts say Israel's continued presence in south Lebanon is creating a "bleak" future as it destroys villages in what it is calling a "buffer zone" and a "Forward Defense Line".
